name: Sofia
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Sofia: IT and outsourcing partner diligence, procurement and real estate risk, and Sofia court support.
hero_lede: Sofia produces close to half of Bulgaria's economic output and hosts its courts, regulators, exchange and a large IT and outsourcing sector. TDSC scopes investigative consulting from Nashville for matters touching the city, working from lawful public sources and coordinating Bulgarian counsel and qualified local professionals.
intro: Sofia is Bulgaria's capital and dominant business centre. According to an Institute for Market Economics analysis reported by the state news agency BTA in February 2026, the Sofia region generated about EUR 46 billion of GDP in 2024, roughly 44 percent of the national total, up from 26 percent in 2000, with per capita output of EUR 35,400, far ahead of any other region. Technology is the city's signature industry: the investment agency Invest Sofia reports more than 100,000 people working in IT, a sector accounting for nearly a quarter of the city economy, alongside a large outsourcing industry in IT, business process and research and development services. The national regulators, Bulgarian Stock Exchange and highest courts are all in the city.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Sofia because the city is where foreign companies place development centres, contract outsourcing providers, buy property and bid for public contracts. A buyer of a Sofia software house needs to know who really owns it and whether key staff or code are encumbered; a client outsourcing customer operations needs assurance about a provider's owners and data handling; a lender to a residential or office project needs the developer's history. Public procurement and EU-funded projects, administered largely from the capital, carry integrity risks that investors and partners must assess before committing.

matters.title: Software company acquisition diligence
matters.text: Foreign buyers acquire Sofia software houses and development centres for talent and products. We verify ownership through the Commercial Register, map related entities and founders' other interests, and review litigation and media, so that a buyer understands who controls the business and what disputes or obligations come with it.

matters.title: Outsourcing provider due diligence
matters.text: Sofia's IT, business process and knowledge process outsourcing firms handle clients' systems and personal data. We examine providers' owners, managers, financial filings, litigation and reputation, and identify subcontracting chains, so clients can judge integrity, stability and data protection risk before signing service agreements.

matters.title: Public procurement and EU funds
matters.text: Contracts awarded by ministries and the capital municipality, including EU-funded projects, attract scrutiny for conflicts of interest and connected bidders. We research bidders, subcontractors and their owners against public procurement and corporate records, helping partners and lenders identify integrity red flags before joining a consortium.

matters.title: Real estate developer backgrounds
matters.text: Residential and office development in Sofia has drawn local and foreign capital. We trace developers' corporate histories, related companies, property and court records and prior projects, helping lenders, buyers and investors judge whether a developer has delivered before and whether disputes or insolvency proceedings surround its group.

matters.title: Litigation and asset research
matters.text: Commercial claims against Bulgarian counterparties are often litigated or enforced in Sofia. We assist Bulgarian counsel with research on defendants' corporate interests, registered property and connected persons, supporting decisions on interim measures, enforcement and settlement in Bulgarian courts or arbitration.

local_context.title: Courts sitting in Sofia
local_context.text: Sofia hosts the Supreme Court of Cassation and the Supreme Administrative Court, as well as appellate and first-instance courts for the capital. Larger commercial disputes involving Sofia-based parties are typically heard at first instance by the Sofia City Court, with appeals to the Sofia Court of Appeal and final review by the Supreme Court of Cassation. Court records are partly searchable online, but access to case files is generally limited to parties and their lawyers, so litigation research is coordinated with Bulgarian counsel.

local_context.title: Arbitration Court at the BCCI
local_context.text: The Arbitration Court at the Bulgarian Chamber of Commerce and Industry, based in Sofia, is the country's principal arbitral institution and handles domestic and international commercial disputes. Following 2025 reforms to the Arbitration Act, arbitral institutions must register with the Ministry of Justice, a change intended to curb abusive arbitration. Investigators supporting a Sofia arbitration work through the parties' counsel and the tribunal's procedural orders on evidence.

local_context.title: Registers and the Registry Agency
local_context.text: The Registry Agency, headquartered in Sofia, maintains the electronic Commercial Register and Register of Non-Profit Legal Entities and the Property Register. Company particulars, managers, owners, filed annual accounts and declared beneficial ownership details are central sources for Sofia matters. Full company files require electronic identification, and the scope of public access to beneficial ownership data has changed since 2022, so it is checked for each engagement.

local_context.title: Financial regulators in the capital
local_context.text: The Financial Supervision Commission, operating since 2003 and accountable to the National Assembly, supervises the non-banking financial sector, including investment firms, insurers, pension funds and issuers listed on the Bulgarian Stock Exchange in Sofia. Banking supervision rests with the Bulgarian National Bank within European Banking Supervision. Regulatory registers and enforcement decisions from these bodies are useful sources in diligence on financial counterparties.

tdsc_approach: TDSC has no office in Sofia and works on Sofia matters from Nashville. We define the purpose with the client first, whether an acquisition, an outsourcing contract, a procurement consortium, a property loan or a dispute, and confirm the lawful basis under the GDPR and Bulgaria's Personal Data Protection Act. Research draws on the Commercial Register, Property Register, procurement records, court databases, regulatory registers and Bulgarian-language media, read in the original. Bulgaria has no dedicated licensing regime for private investigators that we have identified, so any local enquiries are coordinated through Bulgarian counsel and qualified local professionals. Reports state sources and confidence levels and separate verified facts from inference.

faqs.q: How can we confirm who owns a Sofia IT company?
faqs.a: The Commercial Register shows managers, partners or sole owners, share capital, filed accounts and declared beneficial owners for Bulgarian companies. Where owners are foreign holding companies, we follow the chain into the relevant foreign registers. We compare registered ownership with public statements, media and court records to identify nominees or undisclosed interests.

faqs.q: What should we check before contracting a Sofia outsourcing provider?
faqs.a: We look at ownership and management, financial filings and trends, litigation, insolvency and enforcement history, regulatory issues, and reputational sources in Bulgarian and English. We also check whether the provider relies on subcontractors or related entities. The aim is to confirm the provider's stability and integrity before it handles your systems or personal data.

faqs.q: Where are commercial disputes in Sofia heard?
faqs.a: Larger commercial cases are generally heard at first instance by the Sofia City Court, with appeals to the Sofia Court of Appeal and final review by the Supreme Court of Cassation. Many contracts instead refer disputes to the Arbitration Court at the Bulgarian Chamber of Commerce and Industry. Bulgarian counsel advises on forum; we support their evidence needs.

faqs.q: Can you assess integrity risk in a Sofia public procurement bid?
faqs.a: Yes. We research the contracting authority's past awards, the bidders and subcontractors, their owners and managers, and any links between them or to public officials disclosed in public records and media. We report red flags such as recurring winners or connected bidders so the client and its counsel can decide whether to proceed.

Our research covers Bulgarian-language sources, including registers, court decisions and regional and national media, and key documents are translated for the client. Where interviews or on-the-ground enquiries are required in Sofia, they are carried out by qualified Bulgarian professionals coordinated with local counsel, and TDSC does not represent itself as a Bulgarian firm.
